  "title": "Setting up for the new year",
  "body": "Your help has been critical to getting Firefox for Android (aka Fenix) this far, and it’s been amazing and continues to grow. We thank you for your contribution, suggestions and feedback to get to where we are now.  We are excited about recent enhancements that have been added to Firefox for Android and we want the momentum to continue.\nTo help us keep growing, and to make sure your input gets seen and stays effective, we're going to be cleaning up the issue database for Fenix.  The volume of issues, combined with having limited time to review and tag them properly, has created a situation where there are currently more than 2000+ open tickets. Most of these issues have been inactive for several months and they reference versions of Fenix that are no longer available. \n\n**### A new beginning**\n\nTo get the Fenix project to a point where we can act quickly on timely feedback from the community, we need to get out from under this backlog so that we can effectively address our current issues in the Github repository and deliver the features our community is asking for. Community involvement plays a large role in our development and planning process, and we closely follow the forums and other feedback channels.\n\nWe are taking the following steps in order to turn this repository into an up-to-date,  functional issue tracker for bug reports:\n\n1. The issue templates have been updated as a guide on what information you need to provide when submitting tickets in GitHub:\n\n- 🐞 Bug report: Create a report to help us improve\n- ⭐️ Feature request: Suggest an idea for this project\n- 💻 Web content issue report: Create an issue specifically about something wrong with web content while using Fenix\n- ⛏ Investigative Spike: Create an investigation spike\n- 📈 Telemetry User Story: Create a telemetry user story, assigned to an Epic to track telemetry\n- 💔 Intermittent UI Test Issue: Create an issue to help log a UI test failure\n- 👩🏻‍💻 User Story: Create a user story for an epic\n\n\n2. Issues that have no activity or updates after August 30, 2020 will be closed by an automated process as part of this cleanup effort.\n\n**### Out with the old, in with the new and improved**\n\nUsers are welcome to re-submit bug reports that follow the updated issue template and that still affect the current release of Firefox for Android (aka Fenix). By re-submitting valid issues with up-to-date reproduction steps, the developers will be better equipped to solve any underlying problems. Please include the legacy issue ID in your new submission if there is important context available in the old thread.\n\nWe need the community to help us with this step, and we sincerely appreciate your participation in this cleanup effort.\nWe believe that these actions will improve the development cycle and make the process easier to follow for everyone involved. We apologize in advance for the flood of email notifications, but the pain is temporary and a brighter future awaits.\n\n┆Issue is synchronized with this [Jira Task](https://mozilla-hub.atlassian.net/browse/FNXV2-9341)\n",

      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "Yikes. This stale bot means that every issue on the backlog or even untriaged will just be closed and forgotten. I guess it means that we won't see 15 year old bugs like Bugzilla, but it's not nice to see as a user waiting for improvements to come to Firefox. \r\n\r\nIt's not like I can go and search though every issue I've given a thumbs up to on the Fenix repo to make sure that they won't be closed: https://github.com/isaacs/github/issues/607\r\n\r\nWhen I cared, I would point out duplicates of issues. I don't really care anymore. And while I understand that with many open-source projects on GitHub that there are a lot of duplicate issues, spam, and completely unfeasible requests, I really think that this will just end up in my favourite issues getting closed without any activity from Mozilla employees. I hope you understand my perspective here. I don't feel that excited about Firefox anymore and so I don't care to look for all of the issues I cared about. \r\n\r\n>Issues that have no activity or updates after August 30, 2020 will be closed by an automated process as part of this cleanup effort.\r\n\r\nAnd why that date? Why not sometime AFTER your announcement? And again, there are many issues, including #7325 (one of mine lol), which have not gotten any real activity but are perfectly fine feature requests. Hell, that one is already on _all_ desktop browsers! What is there left to say from someone outside of Mozilla? That issue has been there for a year and a half. "
    },

If that is the case, there are still some valid feature requests that would be affected by this, e.g. see the feature requests mentioned in #13302.\r\n\r\nIssues tagged \"feature-requests\" are not included in this. Those will be kept open and re-evaluated in terms of priority for future work."

    {
      "id": 922145180,
      "url": "https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/fenix/issues/17373#issuecomment-922145180",
      "created_at": "2021-09-18T00:23:43Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-09-18T01:03:31Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "I find it incredibly rude to make volunteer issue reporters fight stale bots all the time. Someone invests time to write up a bug description and reproducer, and along comes some program - not even a human - to throw it out. I can only take it as a sign that contributions in the form of issue reports are not welcome.\r\n\r\nI know, issues are very small \"contributions\" that won't benefit the project much, but it just feels disrespectful to me to close/wontfix them purely on the speculation that they MIGHT not be present on the latest version.\r\n\r\n>We apologize in advance for the flood of email notifications, but the pain is temporary and a brighter future awaits.\r\n\r\nIs it though? The number of notifications I get from bots tagging bugs as stale that are very much still present (across all of github) only went up over the past years.\r\n\r\nUsually, **users are discouraged from writing comments that don't add something new to the discussion. Therefore issues that still exist exactly as described naturally get no activity.** Simultaneously, the stale bot assumes issues without activity are no longer relevant. How is this not a conflict?\r\nShould we now comment \"+1 same for me\" and \"Still not fixed on latest version!!!11\" on all issues we come across?"
    },
    {
      "id": 922883887,
      "url": "https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/fenix/issues/17373#issuecomment-922883887",
      "created_at": "2021-09-20T12:29:00Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@AgentOak I can understand your frustration but this bot really helps the dev team. There are currently more than 1.8k open issues. Having a bot pinging the reporter of old issues to check if the issue is still relevant allows the bot to close outdated ones and promote the issues that are still to be fixed, implemented or discussed during triage.\r\n\r\nThere is no hidden agenda to spam users with notifications or hide the issues to discourage them contributing. The contribution from the community is really precious.\r\n\r\nSee [this comment](https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/fenix/issues/13946#issuecomment-891659003) for more context."
    },
